housing_laws.summary: Minnesota has strong tenant protections including cold weather rule, statutory right to privacy, and limits on landlord entry.

notice_requirements.termination_lease_end: No notice required if lease specifies end date
notice_requirements.nonpayment: 14 days to pay or vacate (No notice for manufactured home parks)
notice_requirements.notes: Written notice required. Email/text only valid if tenant agreed in writing.

security_deposit.notes: Landlord must provide written statement of reasons for withholding any deposit.

rent_control.local_programs: Minneapolis has some affordable housing programs but no broad rent control
rent_control.notes: State law preempts local rent control. Tenant can challenge unreasonable rent increases in court under 'unconscionable' standard.

tenant_remedies.notes: Tenant must give 14 days notice for repairs. Amount deducted cannot exceed $500 or one month's rent.

repairs.cold_weather_rule: Nov 1 - Apr 15: Utility shutoffs prohibited for non-payment if tenant establishes payment plan with utility

landlord_entry.tenant_rights: Tenant can refuse entry without proper notice. Repeated unauthorized entry = landlord harassment.

eviction.timeline: Typically 2-6 weeks from filing to hearing
eviction.expungement: Eviction records can be expunged in certain circumstances

protected_classes: Status with regard to public assistance

housing_laws.landlord_tenant_act: California Civil Code §§1940-1954.05; Code of Civil Procedure §1161-1179a (unlawful detainer)
housing_laws.summary: California has strong tenant protections including the implied warranty of habitability, AB 1482 rent cap (2019), and just-cause eviction requirements for most rentals.

notice_requirements.termination_month_to_month: 30 days if tenant <1 year; 60 days if 1+ years (CC §1946.1)
notice_requirements.termination_lease_end: No notice required if lease specifies end date
notice_requirements.notes: Written notice required. AB 1482 requires just cause for eviction after 12 months of tenancy.

security_deposit.limit: 1 month rent (AB 12, effective July 1, 2024 — previously 2 months unfurnished, 3 months furnished)
withholding_allowed: Cost of restoration if allowed by lease
security_deposit.notes: Landlord must provide itemized statement with receipts for amounts >$126. AB 12 (2024) reduced deposit limit to 1 month for most rentals.

rent_control.local_programs: Local rent control in Los Angeles, San Francisco, Oakland, Berkeley, San Jose, West Hollywood, and others; Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act (1995) limits local control on single-family homes and post-1995 construction
rent_control.notes: AB 1482 (2019) caps rent increases at 5% + CPI, max 10% annually. Exempts single-family homes (with specific notice) and properties <15 years old.

repairs.emergency_repairs: Reasonable time — typically 24-72 hours depending on severity
repairs.warranty_of_habitability: CC §1941.1 — implied warranty that premises are fit for human habitation

tenant_remedies.notes: Tenant must give landlord reasonable notice (typically 30 days) before deducting. Repair-and-deduct limited to 1 month's rent.

landlord_entry.notice_period: 24 hours reasonable notice (CC §1954); 48 hours for move-out inspection
landlord_entry.tenant_rights: Tenant can refuse entry without proper notice. Repeated unauthorized entry = landlord harassment (CC §1940.2).

eviction.timeline: Typically 4-8 weeks from notice to lockout; faster in some counties
eviction.expungement: Eviction records can be sealed if case dismissed or tenant wins (CCP §1161.2)

discrimination.statute: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (Gov Code §12955); Unruh Civil Rights Act
discrimination.enforcement_agency: CA Department of Fair Employment and Housing (DFEH)

housing_laws.landlord_tenant_act: NY Real Property Law (RPL) Article 7; RPAPL Article 7; Multiple Dwelling Law; NYC Housing Maintenance Code
housing_laws.summary: New York has strong tenant protections including the Warranty of Habitability, rent stabilization for ~1M NYC apartments, and the Housing Stability and Tenant Protection Act (HSTPA) of 2019.

notice_requirements.nonpayment: 14 days to pay or vacate (RPAPL §711(2); HSTPA 2019)
notice_requirements.lease_violation: 10 days to cure, then 30 days to vacate (RPAPL §711(1))
notice_requirements.termination_month_to_month: 30 days notice if tenant <1 year; 60 days if 1-2 years; 90 days if 2+ years (RPL §232-a, §232-b)
notice_requirements.termination_lease_end: No notice required if lease specifies end date
notice_requirements.notes: Written notice required. HSTPA 2019 eliminated the ability to use rent demand without 14-day notice.

security_deposit.interest_rate: Annual interest on deposits in buildings with 6+ units (RPL §7-106); tenant entitled to 1% of deposit annually
security_deposit.notes: Landlord must provide itemized statement of any withholding within 14 days or forfeit right to withhold.

rent_control.local_programs: NYC Rent Stabilization (~1M apartments), NYC Rent Control (~22K apartments), ETPA (Emergency Tenant Protection Act) adopted by some downstate municipalities
rent_control.notes: HSTPA 2019 removed vacancy deregulation and high-rent deregulation. Rent stabilization now continues with each new tenancy. Upstate NY generally has no rent control.

repairs.warranty_of_habitability: RPL §235-b — implied warranty that premises are fit for human habitation

tenant_remedies.hp_action: Tenant can file HP Action in Housing Court for repairs (CPLR Article 7-A)

landlord_entry.notice_period: Reasonable notice — typically 24 hours (no specific statutory period statewide; NYC Housing Maintenance Code implies reasonable)
landlord_entry.tenant_rights: Tenant can refuse entry without reasonable notice. Repeated unauthorized entry may constitute harassment under NYC Admin Code §27-2004.

eviction.court: Housing Court (NYC) or Local Justice Court / City Court (upstate)
eviction.timeline: Typically 3-6 months from notice to warrant of eviction; NYC longer due to backlog
eviction.expungement: Eviction records can be sealed if case dismissed or tenant wins (RPAPL §749(3); HSTPA 2019)

discrimination.statute: NY State Human Rights Law (Executive Law §296); NYC Human Rights Law (Admin Code §8-107)
discrimination.enforcement_agency: NY Division of Human Rights; NYC Commission on Human Rights

housing_laws.summary: Texas has limited tenant protections compared to most states. No statewide rent control, minimal notice requirements, and landlord-friendly eviction process.

notice_requirements.nonpayment: 3 days to pay or vacate (unless lease specifies different period; TPC §92.206)
notice_requirements.lease_violation: Reasonable time per lease terms; no specific statutory cure period
notice_requirements.termination_lease_end: No notice required if lease specifies end date
notice_requirements.illegal_activity: Per lease terms; no specific statutory period
notice_requirements.notes: Written notice required for nonpayment. Many leases waive the 3-day period — read your lease carefully.

security_deposit.notes: Landlord must provide itemized description of damages within 30 days. Tenant must provide forwarding address in writing or landlord has no obligation to return.

rent_control.local_programs: None — rent control prohibited by state law (TPC §92.021)
rent_control.notes: Texas expressly prohibits cities and counties from enacting rent control. Only the governor can authorize rent control during a disaster, and it expires when the disaster declaration ends.

repairs.emergency_repairs: 7 days to remedy after written notice (TPC §92.056)
repairs.warranty_of_habitability: TPC §92.052 — landlord must make repairs to conditions that affect health or safety

tenant_remedies.notes: Tenant must give landlord written notice and reasonable time (7 days). If landlord fails to repair, tenant can: repair-and-deduct (limited to 1 month's rent or $500, whichever is greater), terminate lease, or sue for damages (TPC §92.056).

landlord_entry.tenant_rights: No statutory right to notice. Tenant can negotiate notice in lease. Repeated unreasonable entry may constitute harassment but hard to prove without lease provision.

eviction.court: Justice Court (forcible detainer); County Court for appeal
eviction.timeline: Typically 2-4 weeks from notice to writ of possession; fastest in the country
eviction.expungement: Eviction records generally public for 7 years; limited sealing available

discrimination.statute: Texas Fair Housing Act (Gov Code §301); Federal Fair Housing Act
discrimination.enforcement_agency: Texas Workforce Commission - Civil Rights Division; HUD

housing_laws.landlord_tenant_act: Florida Statutes Chapter 83, Part II (Residential Tenancies)
housing_laws.summary: Florida is landlord-friendly. No rent control, 3-day notice for nonpayment, and limited tenant remedies for repairs.

notice_requirements.nonpayment: 3 days to pay or vacate (excluding weekends and legal holidays; FL Stat §83.56(3))
notice_requirements.lease_violation: 7 days to cure or vacate (FL Stat §83.56(2)(b))
notice_requirements.termination_lease_end: No notice required if lease specifies end date
notice_requirements.illegal_activity: Per lease terms; 7 days notice for non-curable violations (FL Stat §83.56(2)(a))
notice_requirements.notes: Written notice required. 3-day notice excludes weekends and legal holidays — count carefully.

security_deposit.return_deadline: 15 days (no claim) or 30 days (with claim) after lease ends and tenant provides forwarding address (FL Stat §83.49(3))
security_deposit.interest_rate: Landlord must pay 5% interest or 75% of passbook rate on deposits held (FL Stat §83.49(3))
security_deposit.notes: Landlord must give 30 days' written notice by certified mail of intent to impose claim. Tenant must object within 15 days or claim is forfeited.

rent_control.local_programs: None — rent control prohibited by state law (FL Stat §125.01055, §166.0431)
rent_control.notes: Florida expressly prohibits local rent control. Only the governor can authorize temporary rent control during a declared housing emergency.

landlord_duties: Keep plumbing, heating, electrical in working order
repairs.emergency_repairs: 7 days to remedy after written notice (FL Stat §83.56(1))
repairs.warranty_of_habitability: FL Stat §83.51 — landlord must comply with applicable building/housing codes

tenant_remedies.notes: Tenant must give landlord 7 days' written notice. If landlord fails to repair, tenant can: withhold rent (FL Stat §83.60), terminate lease, or sue for damages. Tenant must allow landlord access for repairs.

landlord_entry.tenant_rights: Tenant can refuse entry without proper notice. Landlord cannot abuse right of access or use it to harass tenant (FL Stat §83.53(5)).

eviction.timeline: Typically 2-4 weeks from 3-day notice to writ of possession
eviction.expungement: Eviction records generally public; limited sealing available if case dismissed

discrimination.statute: Florida Fair Housing Act (FL Stat §760.23); Federal Fair Housing Act
discrimination.enforcement_agency: Florida Commission on Human Relations; HUD

housing_laws.landlord_tenant_act: 765 ILCS 705 (Mobile Home Landlord-Tenant), 740 ILCS 700 (Security Deposit Return Act); Chicago Residential Landlord and Tenant Ordinance (RLTO) for Chicago
housing_laws.summary: Illinois has moderate tenant protections statewide with stronger protections in Chicago (RLTO), Cook County, and Evanston. No statewide rent control.

notice_requirements.nonpayment: 5 days to pay or vacate (735 ILCS 5/9-209)
notice_requirements.lease_violation: 10 days to remedy or vacate (735 ILCS 5/9-210)
notice_requirements.termination_lease_end: No notice required if lease specifies end date
notice_requirements.notes: Written notice required. Chicago RLTO may require longer notice periods for some terminations.

security_deposit.limit: No statewide limit; Chicago RLTO limits to 1.5 months for some units
security_deposit.return_deadline: 30 days (itemized list of damages) or 45 days (full refund) after lease ends and tenant provides forwarding address (765 ILCS 710/1)
security_deposit.interest_rate: Landlord must pay interest on deposits held 6+ months in buildings with 25+ units (Chicago RLTO requires interest on all deposits in covered units)
security_deposit.notes: Chicago RLTO requires landlord to provide receipts for all deductions. Failure to comply = damages equal to deposit amount + attorney fees.

rent_control.local_programs: None — rent control prohibited by state law (IL Rent Control Preemption Act, 50 ILCS 825)
rent_control.notes: Illinois expressly prohibits local rent control. Only the General Assembly can authorize rent control, and it has not done so despite repeated attempts.

repairs.emergency_repairs: 14 days to remedy after written notice (765 ILCS 755/2 — Residential Tenant's Right to Repair Act)
repairs.warranty_of_habitability: Implied warranty under Illinois common law (case law: Glasoe v. Trinkle, 2008); Chicago RLTO §5-12-070

tenant_remedies.notes: Tenant must give landlord 14 days' written notice. If landlord fails to repair, tenant can: repair-and-deduct (up to $500 or half month's rent, whichever is greater), terminate lease, or sue for damages. Chicago RLTO provides additional remedies.

landlord_entry.notice_period: 2 days notice (Chicago RLTO §5-12-030); no specific statewide statutory period
landlord_entry.tenant_rights: Tenant can refuse entry without proper notice. Chicago RLTO requires 2 days notice. Repeated unauthorized entry may constitute harassment.

eviction.timeline: Typically 3-6 weeks from notice to eviction; Chicago longer due to backlog
eviction.expungement: Eviction records can be sealed if case dismissed or tenant wins (735 ILCS 5/9-121.9; effective 2021)

discrimination.statute: Illinois Human Rights Act (775 ILCS 5/3); Chicago Fair Housing Ordinance
discrimination.enforcement_agency: Illinois Department of Human Rights; Chicago Commission on Human Relations

housing_laws.landlord_tenant_act: Pennsylvania Landlord and Tenant Act of 1951 (68 P.S. § 250.101 et seq.)
housing_laws.summary: Pennsylvania has moderate tenant protections. Philadelphia and Pittsburgh have stronger local ordinances. State law governs security deposits, eviction procedure, and landlord duties.

notice_requirements.termination_month_to_month: 15 days written notice required (PA is unusual — only 15 days for month-to-month)
notice_requirements.termination_lease_end: No notice required if lease specifies end date
notice_requirements.nonpayment: 10 days written notice to pay or vacate (Landlord and Tenant Act § 250.503)
notice_requirements.lease_violation: 15 days to remedy or vacate for residential leases
notice_requirements.illegal_activity: Lease may allow shorter notice for illegal activity; otherwise 15 days
notice_requirements.notes: Written notice required. Philadelphia requires 30 days for month-to-month termination under local ordinance.

security_deposit.limit: No more than 2 months' rent for first year; 1 month thereafter
security_deposit.return_deadline: 30 days after lease ends and tenant provides forwarding address
security_deposit.notes: Interest on deposits held 2+ years must be paid to tenant. Landlord must place deposit in escrow account.

rent_control.local_programs: No statewide rent control. Pennsylvania prohibits local rent control except where grandfathered.
rent_control.notes: State law preempts local rent control. Tenant can challenge unconscionable rent increases in court.

landlord_duties: Keep unit weatherproof and structurally sound

tenant_remedies.notes: Tenant can withhold rent if landlord fails to make essential repairs after written notice. Repair-and-deduct is not explicitly authorized by statute but is sometimes permitted by courts.

repairs.emergency_repairs: Varies by severity; typically 24-72 hours for heating/hot water
repairs.cold_weather_rule: No statewide cold weather rule, but utilities must follow PA Public Utility Commission winter shutoff protections for low-income households

landlord_entry.tenant_rights: Tenant can refuse entry without proper notice. Repeated unauthorized entry may constitute harassment.

eviction.court: Magisterial District Court (initial filing); Court of Common Pleas for appeals
eviction.timeline: Typically 3-6 weeks from filing to judgment; 10-21 days for writ of possession
tenant_defenses: Landlord failed to maintain unit (implied warranty of habitability)
eviction.expungement: Eviction records generally not expunged in PA; limited exceptions

discrimination.familial_status: Cannot refuse to rent to families with children

housing_laws.landlord_tenant_act: Michigan Landlord and Tenant Relationships Act (MCL § 554.601 et seq.) and Truth in Renting Act (MCL § 554.631 et seq.)
housing_laws.summary: Michigan has moderate tenant protections. Detroit, Ann Arbor, and some other cities have stronger local ordinances. State law governs security deposits, eviction, and landlord duties.

notice_requirements.termination_month_to_month: One rental period (typically 30 days) written notice required
notice_requirements.termination_lease_end: No notice required if lease specifies end date
notice_requirements.nonpayment: 7 days written notice to pay or vacate (MCL § 600.5714(1)(b))
notice_requirements.lease_violation: 30 days to remedy or vacate for most violations
notice_requirements.illegal_activity: 7 days notice for drug-related violations; 24 hours for serious crimes
notice_requirements.notes: Written notice required. Detroit requires additional notice periods under local ordinance.

security_deposit.return_deadline: 30 days after lease ends and tenant provides forwarding address
security_deposit.notes: Landlord must send itemized list within 30 days. Tenant must respond within 7 days to dispute. Michigan has strict procedural requirements — failure to comply forfeits landlord's right to withhold.

rent_control.local_programs: No statewide rent control. Michigan prohibits local rent control.
rent_control.notes: State law preempts local rent control. Tenant can challenge unconscionable rent increases in court.

landlord_duties: Keep unit weatherproof and structurally sound

tenant_remedies.notes: Tenant can withhold rent if landlord fails to make essential repairs after reasonable notice. Repair-and-deduct not explicitly authorized by statute but sometimes permitted by courts.

repairs.emergency_repairs: Varies by severity; typically 24-72 hours for heating/hot water
repairs.cold_weather_rule: No statewide cold weather rule, but Michigan utilities must follow MPSC winter shutoff protections for low-income households (Nov 1 - Mar 31)

landlord_entry.tenant_rights: Tenant can refuse entry without proper notice. Repeated unauthorized entry may constitute harassment.

eviction.court: District Court (initial filing); Circuit Court for appeals
eviction.timeline: Typically 3-5 weeks from filing to judgment; 10 days for writ of possession
tenant_defenses: Landlord failed to maintain unit (implied warranty of habitability)
eviction.expungement: Eviction records generally not expunged in MI; limited exceptions

notice_requirements.illegal_activity: Per lease terms; expedited for drug-related violations

security_deposit.limit: 1.5 months' rent for month-to-month; 2 months' rent for longer leases

repairs.emergency_repairs: Varies by severity; typically 24-72 hours for heating/hot water
repairs.cold_weather_rule: No statewide cold weather rule; GA Public Service Commission winter shutoff protections for low-income households

landlord_entry.tenant_rights: Tenant can refuse entry without proper notice. Repeated unauthorized entry may constitute harassment.

eviction.court: Magistrate Court (initial filing); Superior Court for appeals
eviction.timeline: Typically 2-3 weeks from filing to judgment; 7 days for writ of possession
eviction.expungement: Eviction records generally not expunged in GA; limited exceptions

discrimination.familial_status: Cannot refuse to rent to families with children
